Samsung announced it is allocating over half of its 4-nanometer foundry capacity to high-bandwidth memory base dies, raising concerns about future supply competition. Meanwhile, investor Michael Burry expanded short positions in Micron and semiconductor exchange-traded funds on expectations that memory shortages are cyclical rather than structural, CNBC reported.When benchmark bond yields rise, semiconductor valuations face mechanical headwinds because investors heavily discount cash flows projected years into the future. Paired with expanding foundry capacity and looming supply additions, higher capital costs make investors less willing to pay premium multiples for cyclical hardware makers until end-market demand visibility clears.
